title: Agent context compaction: what a summary forgets, and who checks it
summary: When a long-running agent fills its context window it rewrites its own history into a summary. How compaction works across Claude Code, the Claude API and Codex, what measured summaries drop — specifics, file trails, standing instructions, failure signals, and themselves over repeated passes — and why both METR's and Anthropic's October 2026 red-teams found the summary to be a monitoring blind spot.

topics: deep dive: agent context compaction — what a summary forgets
concepts_taught: agent context compaction: replacing the history with a model-written summary when the window fills, and why it is a lossy, editorial rewrite rather than paging — the successor shares no memory with the agent that wrote the note (Codex's prefix calls it 'another language model')

what compaction summaries measurably drop: specifics in favor of gist (Factory's 401-endpoint example), the artifact trail as the weakest probe dimension for every method, and standing instructions, which stop binding once summarized (Claude docs; the OpenClaw inbox case)

context collapse under repeated compaction: re-summarizing a summary drifts toward the generic (brevity bias; ACE's 18,282-to-122-token collapse scoring below no context), and delta/anchored merges into fixed sections as the fix

observation masking versus LLM summarization: replacing old tool outputs with placeholders matches summarization's solve rate at lower cost, and summaries lengthen trajectories, plausibly by hiding failure signals

the compaction summary as a monitoring blind spot: attacks split across compaction seams, forged user intent in the summary treated as trusted context, turn-end-triggered monitors postponed indefinitely, and why robust defense means the monitor reading across boundaries
